exampleGloss.en: Goodbye, all the best to you.
Thank you very much, that's very kind.

exampleGloss.zh: 不好意思，洗手間在哪裡？
exampleGloss.en: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

exampleEs: Lo siento, no puedo ir hoy.

exampleGloss.en: I'm sorry, I can't go today.

gloss.en: excuse me (passing by); if you'll excuse me

exampleGloss.zh: 不好意思借過，我要出去。

exampleGloss.en: —My name is Ana. —Nice to meet you.

exampleEs: El señor Ramírez es mi profesor.

exampleGloss.zh: 拉米雷斯先生是我的老師。

exampleGloss.en: How do you say "book" in Spanish?

exampleEs: No sé dónde está la calle.

exampleGloss.zh: 我不知道那條街在哪裡。
exampleGloss.en: I don't know where the street is.

note.zh: 在基多所在的 Sierra 高地，usted 的使用比多數教材預期得更廣，朋友甚至家人之間也常用。
note.en: In the Sierra highlands around Quito, usted is used far more widely than most textbooks suggest — between friends and even within families.

note.zh: 拉丁美洲的第二人稱複數一律用 ustedes，完全不使用西班牙的 vosotros。
note.en: Throughout Latin America the second-person plural is always ustedes; Spain's vosotros is not used at all.

exampleEs: Mi madre trabaja en un hospital.

exampleGloss.en: My mother works at a hospital.

genderNote.zh: 注意重音：papá（爸爸）跟 papa（馬鈴薯）只差一個重音符號，意思完全不同。
genderNote.en: Watch the accent: papá (dad) and papa (potato) differ by one accent mark and mean completely different things.

exampleGloss.en: My dad is forty years old.

exampleEs: Tengo un hermano y una hermana.

exampleGloss.zh: 我有一個兄弟和一個姊妹。
exampleGloss.en: I have one brother and one sister.

exampleEs: Mi hermana estudia en la universidad.

exampleGloss.en: My sister studies at the university.

exampleEs: Ana es una amiga de mi hermana.

exampleGloss.en: Ana is a friend of my sister's.

exampleEs: La mujer del sombrero es mi tía.

exampleGloss.zh: 戴帽子的那位女士是我阿姨。
exampleGloss.en: The woman in the hat is my aunt.
The boy is five years old.
The girl is reading a book.

genderNote.zh: 陰陽同形：男生用 el estudiante，女生用 la estudiante，字尾不變。
genderNote.en: Same form for both genders: el estudiante (male), la estudiante (female); the ending doesn't change.

exampleEs: La clase es a las tres.

exampleGloss.en: There are four of us in my family.
The boy is five years old.

exampleEs: Trabajo seis días a la semana.

exampleGloss.en: I work six days a week.

exampleEs: Son las ocho de la mañana.

exampleGloss.en: I live on the ninth floor.
My sister is eleven years old.

exampleEs: Hay trece estudiantes en la clase.

exampleGloss.en: There are thirteen students in the class.
My brother is eighteen years old.

exampleEs: Hay diecinueve libros en la mesa.

exampleGloss.en: There are nineteen books on the table.
My dad is forty years old.
My grandmother is seventy years old.

exampleEs: Hay ochenta sillas en la sala.

exampleGloss.en: There are eighty chairs in the hall.

exampleEs: El carro rojo es de mi papá.

exampleGloss.zh: 那台紅色的車是我爸爸的。
exampleGloss.en: The red car belongs to my dad.
The yellow taxi is over there.

exampleEs: La casa blanca es muy grande.

exampleGloss.en: The white house is very big.

exampleEs: La niña tiene un vestido rosado.

exampleGloss.zh: 那個女孩有一件粉紅色洋裝。
exampleGloss.en: The girl has a pink dress.

note.zh: 拉美普遍用 rosado；西班牙較常說 rosa。
note.en: Latin America generally says rosado; Spain more often says rosa.

note.zh: 拉美常用 café 表示棕色；西班牙用 marrón。
note.en: Latin America commonly uses café for brown; Spain uses marrón.

exampleEs: El lunes tengo clase de español.

exampleGloss.zh: 星期一我有西班牙文課。
exampleGloss.en: On Monday I have Spanish class.
On Thursday I'm going to the market.
On Saturday I study at home.

exampleEs: El domingo como con mi familia.

exampleGloss.en: On Sunday I eat with my family.
I didn't go to work yesterday.

genderNote.zh: 字尾是 -a 卻是陽性（el día），是必須背下來的例外。
genderNote.en: Ends in -a but is masculine (el día) — an exception you have to memorise.

exampleGloss.en: Good morning, how's your day going?
I have a lot of work this month.

genderNote.zh: 務必打出 ñ：año 是「年」，而 ano 是「肛門」，差一個字母意思天差地遠。
genderNote.en: Always type the ñ: año means "year", while ano means "anus". One letter, very different meaning.

genderNote.zh: 陰性名詞但單數要配 el（el agua fría），因為字首是重音的 a-。複數恢復 las aguas。
genderNote.en: A feminine noun that takes el in the singular (el agua fría), because it starts with a stressed a-. The plural goes back to las aguas.

exampleEs: Un vaso de agua, por favor.

exampleGloss.en: Would you like coffee with milk?

note.zh: 拉美說 jugo；西班牙說 zumo。
note.en: Latin America says jugo; Spain says zumo.

exampleGloss.en: I buy bread at the shop.

exampleEs: El almuerzo tiene arroz y pollo.

exampleGloss.en: I don't eat meat on Mondays.

exampleEs: En la costa el pescado es fresco.

exampleGloss.en: On the coast the fish is fresh.

exampleEs: La papa es muy importante en los Andes.

exampleGloss.zh: 馬鈴薯在安地斯地區非常重要。
exampleGloss.en: The potato is very important in the Andes.

note.zh: 拉美說 papa；西班牙說 patata。注意 papa（馬鈴薯）與 papá（爸爸）只差重音。
note.en: Latin America says papa; Spain says patata. Note that papa (potato) and papá (dad) differ only by the accent.

exampleEs: El pan con queso está rico.

genderNote.zh: 通常用陽性（el azúcar），但陰性 la azúcar 也聽得到，兩者都可接受。
genderNote.en: Usually masculine (el azúcar), though la azúcar is also heard; both are acceptable.

exampleEs: El almuerzo es a la una.

note.zh: 厄瓜多常用 guineo 指一般食用香蕉，plátano 則多指要煮的大蕉。
note.en: In Ecuador guineo usually means an ordinary eating banana, while plátano refers to the larger cooking plantain.

exampleEs: Mi casa está cerca del mercado.

exampleGloss.en: My house is near the market.

exampleEs: Los niños están en la escuela.
Voy al trabajo a las ocho.

exampleGloss.en: I go to work at eight.

genderNote.zh: 重音符號在 í 上，把 a 和 i 拆成兩個音節：pa-ís。
genderNote.en: The accent on the í splits a and i into two syllables: pa-ís.

exampleEs: La tienda está en esta calle.

exampleGloss.en: The shop is on this street.
I buy bread at the shop.

exampleEs: Hay un restaurante en la esquina.

exampleGloss.en: There's a restaurant on the corner.

exampleEs: El libro está en la mesa.

exampleGloss.en: The book is on the table.

exampleEs: Hay cuatro sillas en la cocina.

exampleGloss.en: There are four chairs in the kitchen.

exampleGloss.zh: 這是一本西班牙文的書。

exampleEs: Mi teléfono está en la mesa.

exampleGloss.en: My phone is on the table.
I don't have any money today.

exampleEs: El café de Ecuador es muy bueno.
La fruta del mercado es barata.

exampleGloss.en: The fruit at the market is cheap.

exampleEs: En Quito hace frío en la noche.

exampleGloss.en: It's cold in Quito at night.

exampleEs: Ella está contenta con su trabajo.

note.zh: 厄瓜多、哥倫比亞、委內瑞拉等地常用的口語讚美詞。
note.en: A common colloquial term of approval in Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela and elsewhere.

note.zh: 厄瓜多年輕人常用，語感比 chévere 更口語。
note.en: Common among younger speakers in Ecuador; more colloquial in feel than chévere.

note.zh: 源自 Kichwa 的厄瓜多用詞，既可指親兄弟，也可像「哥們」一樣稱呼好友。陰性為 ñaña。
note.en: An Ecuadorian term from Kichwa. It can mean an actual brother or be used like "buddy" for a close friend. The feminine is ñaña.

genderNote.zh: 來自 Kichwa 的 wawa，安地斯地區常用；在加勒比地區 guagua 卻是「公車」，意思完全不同。
genderNote.en: From the Kichwa wawa, common across the Andes. In the Caribbean, however, guagua means "bus" — a completely different word.

note.zh: Kichwa 借詞（wawa＝小孩），厄瓜多、祕魯、玻利維亞的安地斯地區通用。
note.en: A Kichwa loanword (wawa = child), used across the Andean regions of Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia.

exampleGloss.en: I have a hangover, I don't want to eat.

note.zh: 厄瓜多特有詞，其他西語國家多說 resaca。
note.en: Specific to Ecuador; most other Spanish-speaking countries say resaca.

note.zh: 厄瓜多口語，相當於「絕對是」「一定」。
note.en: Ecuadorian colloquial usage, equivalent to "definitely" or "for sure".

exampleGloss.en: I'll be right there, wait a moment.

note.zh: 語意刻意模糊：可以指「立刻」，也可以指「等一下再說」，實際多久要看語氣與情境。
note.en: Deliberately vague: it can mean "right now" or "in a little while" — how long depends on tone and context.

note.zh: -ito 指小詞在此不是「小」，而是把語氣變柔和、更有禮貌。
note.en: Here the -ito diminutive doesn't mean "small"; it softens the tone and makes the request more polite.

exampleEs: Mi hermano y yo estudiamos español.

exampleGloss.zh: 我哥哥和我學西班牙文。
exampleGloss.en: My brother and I study Spanish.

exampleEs: No como carne porque no me gusta.

exampleGloss.zh: 我不吃肉，因為我不喜歡。
exampleGloss.en: I don't eat meat because I don't like it.

exampleEs: El libro está en la mesa.

exampleGloss.en: The book is on the table.

exampleEs: Un café sin azúcar, por favor.

exampleGloss.zh: 請給我一杯不加糖的咖啡。

exampleEs: Este libro es para mi hermana.

exampleGloss.en: This book is for my sister.

exampleEs: Mi casa está cerca del mercado.

exampleGloss.en: My house is near the market.

exampleEs: La universidad está lejos de aquí.

exampleGloss.en: The university is far from here.
When are you going to Cuenca?
I work a lot on Mondays.

exampleEs: Siempre bebo café en la mañana.

exampleGloss.en: I always drink coffee in the morning.

exampleEs: El perro está en la casa.

exampleGloss.en: The dog is in the house.

genderNote.zh: 公貓 el gato、母貓 la gata，字尾隨性別變。
genderNote.en: el gato for a male cat, la gata for a female one — the ending follows the animal's sex.

genderNote.zh: 字尾是 -o 卻是陰性（la mano），是最常被考的例外之一。
genderNote.en: Ends in -o but is feminine (la mano) — one of the most commonly tested exceptions.

exampleEs: Tengo un libro en la mano.

exampleGloss.en: I have a book in my hand.

genderNote.zh: 字尾是 -a 卻是陽性（el problema）。源自希臘文的 -ma 結尾字多為陽性。
genderNote.en: Ends in -a but is masculine (el problema). Nouns of Greek origin ending in -ma are usually masculine.

genderNote.zh: 字尾 -a 但是陽性（el mapa），跟 problema 同一類例外。
genderNote.en: Ends in -a but is masculine (el mapa), same exception class as problema.

exampleEs: El mapa está en la mesa.

exampleGloss.en: The map is on the table.

genderNote.zh: 複數是 luces：字尾 -z 變複數時要改成 -ces。
genderNote.en: The plural is luces: nouns ending in -z change to -ces in the plural.

exampleEs: La luz de la cocina está aquí.

genderNote.zh: 複數是 lápices：-z 要改成 -ces，而且重音符號**保留**（lá-pi-ces 重音在倒數第三音節，這類字一律要標）。
genderNote.en: The plural is lápices: -z becomes -ces, and the accent mark is kept (lá-pi-ces is stressed on the third-from-last syllable, which always takes an accent).
